This document is a curation QC report for the UHN Tsao Lab lung cancer PDX XevaSet, built by the Xevacurate Snakemake pipeline.

Setup

Load The Dataset

The curated object is stored as an RDS file in expected_results/xevaset/.

## XevaSet
## name: Tsao_Lung_2022
## Creation date: Mon Sep 14 18:32:52 2026
## Number of models: 1415
## Number of drugs: 35
## Moleculer dataset: RNASeq, mutation, cnv

The XevaSet bundles model metadata, drug metadata, tumor growth measurements, response summaries, and molecular profiles into one object.

Each row in the model metadata represents one drug-response experiment arm (one mouse/passage under one treatment). parental.model.id links related arms back to the same engrafted tumor line.

Key metadata columns include:

  • model.id: unique drug-experiment model identifier (f<batch>.<modelID>.<engraftment>.<drug>.<mouse>).
  • patient.id: patient-level identifier shared across related arms.
  • drug: normalized treatment name (control for untreated arms).
  • oncotree.code / primary.tumor.site / cancer.type.detailed: clinical annotation.
  • model.type / parental.model.id: parental vs. derivative model lineage.

Response Metric Distributions

AUC, slope, and best.average.response summarize different aspects of tumor growth. Lower best.average.response values indicate stronger inhibition or shrinkage relative to baseline; the long right tail on best.average.response (up to 1.1498^{4}%) reflects a small number of rapidly-progressing control/resistant arms and is worth spot-checking rather than assuming it’s a data error.

Waterfall Plot

Waterfall plots rank models from strongest response to weakest response for a given treatment.

## [1] "dacomitinib"

Model-level view

waterfall()’s own default is group.by = "model.id" (not "patient.id", which is summarizeResponse()’s default elsewhere in this report), so each bar below is one individual model record, not one per patient. Patients contribute very unequal numbers of records for dacomitinib — see the per-patient count in the next panel — so a handful of heavily-replicated patients dominate this view.

Patient-level view

Collapsing to one bar per patient (group.by = "patient.id") requires a summary.stat other than the default ";" — cells with more than one record per patient would otherwise be joined into a non-numeric string and waterfall() would error. Using "mean" gives every patient equal visual weight regardless of how many replicate batches they contributed, at the cost of hiding within-patient spread.
